title: Flip Game
statement:
Two players share a row of symbols `currentState` made only of `+` and `-`. A move takes two neighbouring characters that are both `+` (a `"++"` at some position) and turns them into `"--"`; a player who has no such pair to flip cannot move.

Return every string the row can become after exactly one move from `currentState`, one entry per position where `"++"` can be flipped, in any order. If no move is possible, return an empty list.
notes:
## Intuition

A move is completely described by where its `"++"` sits, so the answers are just one new string for each index where two `+` signs stand side by side. Scanning neighbouring pairs once and building the flipped copy for every match is all it takes; there is no game strategy to compute here (that is the follow-up, Flip Game II).

## Approach

1. Start an empty list `moves`.
2. For every `i` from 1 to the end, look at the pair `currentState[i - 1]` and `currentState[i]`.
3. If both are `+`, build the next state from the text `before` the pair, then `"--"`, then the text `after` it, and push it.
4. Return `moves` (empty when no pair matched).

## Example 1, step by step

For `"++++"`: at `i = 1` the pair is `"++"`, `before = ""`, `after = "++"`, giving `"--++"`. At `i = 2`, `before = "+"`, `after = "+"`, giving `"+--+"`. At `i = 3`, `before = "++"`, `after = ""`, giving `"++--"`. The answer is `["--++", "+--+", "++--"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²) in the worst case: there are up to n - 1 matching pairs and each new string copies n characters.
- Space: O(n²) for the returned strings; O(1) extra besides them.

## Pitfalls

- Pairs overlap: in `"+++"` both the first two and the last two characters can be flipped, so do not skip ahead by two after a match.
- Strings are immutable: build a new string for every move instead of changing one shared copy, or later answers inherit earlier flips.
- Only `"++"` can be flipped; `"+-"`, `"-+"` and `"--"` are not moves, and a string shorter than 2 has none.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `moves` | every state reachable in one move |
| `i` | index of the second character of the pair being checked |
| `before` | the part of `currentState` left of the pair |
| `after` | the part of `currentState` right of the pair |

narration.2: Collect every state that one move can produce.
narration.4: Walk over each pair of neighbouring characters, ending at index i.
narration.5: A move is only possible where both characters of the pair are '+'.
narration.6: Keep the text to the left of the pair unchanged.
narration.7: Keep the text to the right of the pair unchanged.
narration.8: Rebuild the string with this pair flipped to '--' and record it.
narration.11: Return all the possible next states, which is empty if no pair matched.
